submissionTextVerbatim.description:
Smart Site assembles what governs a place, the parcel record, zoning, land use and flood, into one current, cited answer, and gives an AI agent the same answer a person gets in the app.

Coverage is Central Texas: Bastrop, Travis, Williamson, Hays, Caldwell and McLennan counties. Ask about a parcel outside that and the connector reports a miss rather than inventing one.

What you can do here:
- Find a parcel by address or parcel id, or every parcel within a set distance of one, with the result marked when more matched than were returned.
- Open a parcel's on-record facts: zoning district and jurisdiction, land use, flood zone, and where the setbacks and buildable envelope stand, carrying their citations where a source can be linked, and the date each was baked.
- Read the property intelligence report for a parcel.
- Build a screening board from a pasted list of addresses and work it row by row.
- Save parcels, set a status on them, and list what you have saved.

Where a fact is not on record, Smart Site says which kind of nothing it is, reported absent, unknown, not read, or refused, each with a reason, instead of guessing. On many parcels the buildable envelope is a declared refusal rather than a distance, and it says so. It will not invent a setback, a flood zone or a zoning district. It does no valuation, no listings or sold prices, and no owner lookup, and nothing it returns is a boundary survey or a legal record.

Connecting uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE against your Smart Site account, the same sign-in you use in the app. The connector is a door, not a plan: it is available on every plan including Free, and it applies the same limits the app applies. Opening a parcel's full read needs Solo or above, or a 30-day unlock on that parcel. Reading the report needs a paid plan.

staleness.whatWasDoneInstead: Mitigation, not control, and it is named as such. The copy carries no tool count, so an addition cannot falsify it. It states the tier rule as an invariant, 'it applies the same limits the app applies', so P-101 moving screens to Studio cannot falsify it. It names no report menu. staleness.whatARealControlWouldBe: A scheduled job that fetches https://mcp.smartsite.cloud/llms.txt, diffs the tool names and readiness markers against a committed snapshot, and exits non-zero on any difference. Executor: a CI schedule. Trigger: cron, plus every merge touching artifacts/smartsite-mcp. Failure: non-zero exit and a red check. Bypass: a change deployed without passing CI, and a change to the listing itself, which the diff does not read. It is a new build with its own row and it is not this card.
staleness.theCheckerBuiltHereIsNotThat: _inbox/2026-09-02_p88_directory_listing_check.mjs checks the COPY against a hardcoded rule list. It would catch a human reintroducing a forbidden phrase. It has no knowledge of the live tool set and would not have caught either of the two real regressions. Saying so is the point: it is a lint, not a staleness gate.

LESSON: A capability disclosure served BY the product is still a claim, not a measurement. mcp.smartsite.cloud/llms.txt presents export_instrument as live; the production tool returns not_ready because a config value is absent. The disclosure is generated from the readiness field in source, and the refusal comes from a runtime config check the disclosure never consults. Any lane quoting llms.txt as ground truth is quoting main, not production.

A presence-shaped copy check cannot tell a promise from a disclaimer. The first version of the listing checker failed the copy on 'sold price' inside the sentence 'no listings or sold prices', which is the sentence keeping the promise. The fix is polarity awareness plus must-PASS fixtures, not rewording the copy to satisfy a defective instrument.

Anthropic's connector submission is a Team-or-Enterprise-organization action, not an individual one, and it demands a documentation URL, a permanent slug, an icon, a test account, and for an MCP App three to five PNG screenshots. Any future 'list us in a directory' card should check the account tier FIRST, because it gates everything else.

A fenced-block extractor anchored on a bare newline is defeated by a CRLF rewrite, and Python text-mode writes on Windows produce exactly that. Normalize line endings inside the instrument and make it exit non-zero when it extracts fewer blocks than expected, rather than letting it read undefined.
